problem: Let $f$ and $g$ be continuous functions such that ${\int }_{0}^{7}f(x)\,\text{d}x=18,{\int }_{0}^{7}\frac{1}{2}g(x)\,\text{d}x=5,$ and ${\int }_{3}^{7}(f(x)-g(x))\text{d}x=4.$ What is the value of ${\int }_{0}^{3}(f(x)-g(x))\text{d}x?$

activity_context.topic_title: Properties of Definite Integrals Involving the Limits of Integration

feedback.problem: Suppose that $f(x)$ is a  function such that ${\int }_{3}^{11}f(x)\,\text{d}x=13$ and ${\int }_{15}^{11}7\,f(x)\,\text{d}x=21.$ What is the value of ${\int }_{3}^{15}f(x)\,\text{d}x?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let's simplify one of the given integrals:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{15}^{11}7\,f(x)\,\text{d}x & =21 \\ 7{\int }_{15}^{11}\,f(x)\,\text{d}x & =21 \\ -7{\int }_{11}^{15}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =21 \\ {\int }_{11}^{15}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =-3\end{aligned}
$$

Then, from the adjacent intervals rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{3}^{15}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{3}^{11}f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{11}^{15}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =13+(-3) \\  & =10.\end{aligned}
$$
